paper.title_en: Cross-chip transfer in quantum photonic neural networks
paper.abstract_en: Fabrication variability makes it difficult to reuse one set of trained parameters across a batch of quantum photonic chips without additional chip-specific optimization. We examine how device-specific compensation and task tolerance shape cross-chip performance. For squared operator loss, local analysis predicts that reducing own-chip error through compensation incurs an increase in expected loss on independent chips. We use Monte Carlo ensemble training (MC-ENS), informed by an available statistical model of fabrication-induced parameter errors. It optimizes one shared parameter set for each task or target at a given fabrication scale by averaging losses over simulated chip realizations resampled from this model. Numerical simulations of a quantum photonic neural network compare MC-ENS with single-chip training, sharpness-aware training and a covariance-informed variant. For CNOT synthesis and Ising dynamics, MC-ENS reduces mean conditional process infidelity and increases mean postselection probability on unseen chips. In classification, high accuracy can persist despite substantial changes in the optical transformation. The decision-margin analysis shows when fabrication-induced score shifts are likely to change predicted labels. The trained shared parameters can be reused without device-specific retraining on unseen chips drawn from the same fabrication distribution.
